readAloud.text: The Oakridge Community Center will reopen its swimming pool on Monday after two weeks of maintenance. Morning lap swimming will begin at six thirty, and family swim hours will start at four in the afternoon. Members should bring their own towels because towel service will not be available until next month. Lockers near the pool have also been replaced and now require a one-dollar coin that is returned after use. Anyone registered for swimming lessons will receive an updated schedule by email. Please contact the front desk if you do not receive your schedule by Friday.

readAloud.text: Thank you for visiting Pine Street Pharmacy. Prescription pickup is available from eight in the morning until nine at night on weekdays and from nine until six on weekends. Customers who receive a text message saying their order is ready may use the express counter near the entrance. Please bring photo identification when picking up certain medications. The pharmacy also offers free blood pressure checks every Tuesday afternoon. If you have questions about a new prescription, ask to speak with a pharmacist before leaving the store. We are happy to explain dosage instructions and possible side effects.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The Midtown Office Building will conduct a fire safety drill next Thursday at ten thirty in the morning. When the alarm sounds, employees should stop working and use the nearest marked stairway to leave the building. Elevators must not be used during the drill. After exiting, each department should meet at its assigned location in Central Plaza. Supervisors will take attendance before anyone returns inside. The exercise is expected to last about twenty minutes. Visitors who are in the building at the time of the drill should remain with the employee or department they are visiting.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Beginning this month, Brookfield Library is offering free technology help sessions for adults every Wednesday evening. Volunteers can assist with basic smartphone settings, video calls, online forms, and common computer programs. Sessions are held from six to eight and do not require an appointment. Participants should bring the device they want help with, along with any necessary chargers or passwords. For privacy reasons, volunteers cannot access banking information or make purchases for participants. The library also offers longer individual computer lessons on Saturday mornings. Those appointments can be reserved at the information desk.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Welcome to Silver Coast Bicycle Rentals. Bicycles may be rented by the hour or for the entire day, and every rental includes a helmet and lock. Customers must present a valid identification card before receiving a bicycle. Please return equipment to this location at least fifteen minutes before closing time. If you experience a mechanical problem during your ride, call the service number printed on your rental receipt. Our staff can arrange assistance or provide directions to the nearest repair point. For safety, riders should use designated bicycle lanes whenever possible and follow all local traffic rules.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Employees are reminded that enrollment for next year's health insurance plan closes on Friday at five p.m. Anyone who wants to change medical, dental, or family coverage must submit the online form before the deadline. Employees who are satisfied with their current plan do not need to take action unless their family information has changed. Human Resources will hold two question-and-answer sessions this week in Meeting Room 2C. A benefits specialist will also be available by phone each afternoon from one until four. Updated plan descriptions and monthly costs are posted on the employee website.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The Lakeside Farmers Market will celebrate its tenth anniversary this Sunday with additional food stands and live entertainment. The market opens at eight a.m., and a cooking demonstration will begin near the main entrance at eleven. Local musicians will perform during the afternoon, and children can join free craft activities until three o'clock. Visitors are encouraged to bring reusable bags and water bottles. Parking near the market is limited, so a free shuttle will operate every twenty minutes from the community college parking lot. Most vendors accept cards, but carrying some cash is recommended.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Thank you for calling Weston Medical Clinic. Patients with scheduled appointments should arrive ten minutes early and check in at the reception desk on the third floor. If you have cold or flu symptoms, please wear a mask while you are in the waiting area. Same-day appointments may be available for urgent problems, but patients should call before coming to the clinic. Laboratory services are open from seven thirty until four without an appointment. Test results are normally posted in the patient portal within three business days. For emergencies, please contact your local emergency service instead of the clinic.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The Northpoint Hotel will begin renovating its ground-floor restaurant next Monday. During construction, breakfast will be served in the second-floor ballroom from six thirty until ten each morning. Dinner service will be available through room service and at several nearby partner restaurants. Guests may ask the front desk for a list of participating locations and discount offers. Construction work will take place only between nine a.m. and five p.m. to reduce noise during early morning and evening hours. The restaurant is expected to reopen in six weeks with additional seating and a redesigned menu.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: City residents can now register for spring gardening classes at the Botanical Learning Center. Classes cover topics such as balcony gardening, vegetable planting, and caring for indoor plants. Most sessions last ninety minutes and include a short demonstration followed by hands-on practice. Tools and materials are provided, but participants may bring gardening gloves if they prefer. Registration costs fifteen dollars per class, and space is limited to eighteen people. A discounted package is available for anyone who registers for three or more sessions. Complete schedules and instructor information can be found on the center's website.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Starting on September first, Horizon Bank will extend customer service hours at its downtown branch. The branch will open at eight thirty on weekdays and remain open until seven on Thursdays. Saturday hours will continue from nine until one. Customers can meet with financial advisers by appointment for questions about savings, loans, or small-business accounts. Most routine services, including transfers and bill payments, are also available through online banking. The drive-through window will close thirty minutes before the lobby each day. Please check the bank website for holiday schedules before planning your visit.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The Westfield Museum has introduced a new reservation system for weekend visitors. Guests may choose an arrival time online and enter the museum within thirty minutes of that time. Reservations are recommended but are not required when space is available. The permanent galleries remain free, while special exhibitions may require a separate ticket. Large bags must be checked at the coat room near the main entrance. Photography is permitted in most galleries unless a sign says otherwise. Families can borrow free activity kits from the education desk, and guided tours are offered twice each Saturday afternoon.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Our company will replace the printers on the fourth and fifth floors this weekend. The new machines will support color printing, scanning, and secure document release using employee identification cards. Beginning Monday, employees must select the new printer name from their computer settings before sending a document. Instructions will be available beside each machine and on the technology support website. Old printer access will remain active for one week in case of technical problems. Employees who regularly print confidential documents should use the secure release feature and collect papers immediately after printing.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The Harborview Restaurant is now accepting reservations for its annual winter dinner series. Each Friday evening in January, the chef will prepare a four-course menu featuring seasonal ingredients from local farms. Dinner begins at seven, and guests should plan to arrive at least fifteen minutes early. Vegetarian meals are available when requested during booking. Because the menu changes each week, food allergies should also be reported in advance. Reservations require a small deposit that will be applied to the final bill. Cancellations made at least forty-eight hours before dinner will receive a full refund.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Passengers using Central Station should allow extra travel time this weekend because two platforms will be closed for repairs. Trains on the Green Line will depart from Platform 6 instead of Platform 3 from Saturday morning through Sunday evening. Station employees will be available near the ticket machines to answer questions and direct passengers. Electronic signs will display updated platform information throughout the station. Travelers with bicycles should use the north entrance, where the elevators will remain open. Normal platform assignments are expected to resume before the first train on Monday morning.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The university's Career Development Office will hold resume review appointments throughout the month of October. Students may bring a printed resume or upload a digital copy before their appointment. Advisers will provide feedback on organization, wording, and how clearly experience is presented. Each appointment lasts twenty-five minutes and can be held in person or by video call. Students applying for internships are encouraged to schedule early because appointments fill quickly near application deadlines. The office also offers a free online resume checklist and sample documents for students who want to make improvements before meeting with an adviser.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Thank you for shopping at Cedar Home Furnishings. Furniture deliveries are scheduled within a two-hour arrival window, and customers will receive a confirmation message the evening before delivery. Please make sure hallways and entry areas are clear before the delivery team arrives. Standard delivery includes bringing items into the requested room, but assembly may require an additional service fee. If no adult is present at the scheduled time, the delivery may need to be rescheduled. Customers should inspect each item before the team leaves and report visible damage immediately to the delivery supervisor.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The Riverside Theater is looking for volunteers for its summer outdoor performance series. Volunteers help check tickets, guide audience members to seating areas, and answer basic visitor questions. Each volunteer works one four-hour shift and receives a free ticket for a future performance. A short orientation session is required before the first shift. Volunteers must be at least sixteen years old, and anyone under eighteen needs written permission from a parent or guardian. Applications are available online until May fifteenth. Selected volunteers will receive their schedules and orientation details by email at the end of May.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Beginning next week, the Greenway Office Cafeteria will offer mobile ordering during the lunch period. Employees can place an order through the company app between ten thirty and one thirty and choose a pickup time. Orders will be prepared at a separate counter beside the main entrance. The regular cafeteria line will remain open for employees who prefer to order in person. Mobile orders can be changed until fifteen minutes before pickup. To reduce waste, disposable utensils will only be included when requested. The cafeteria plans to add breakfast ordering later this year if the lunch service works well.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The Hilltop Community College bookstore will buy back selected textbooks during final exam week. Students should bring their books and student identification to the buyback desk on the first floor. The amount offered depends on the book's condition and whether it will be used in courses next semester. Books with missing pages or serious water damage cannot be accepted. The bookstore will also accept rental-book returns at the same desk. Students are encouraged to come earlier in the week to avoid long lines. Buyback payments can be issued in cash or added to a campus payment card.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Visitors to Maplewood Park should note that the east parking lot will be closed this Saturday for resurfacing. The west lot and street parking near the recreation center will remain available. Because fewer parking spaces will be open, visitors are encouraged to walk, cycle, or use the city bus if possible. All playgrounds, walking paths, and sports fields will remain open during normal hours. Work is expected to finish by Sunday evening, but the schedule may change if it rains. Updated parking information will be posted at each park entrance and on the city's recreation website.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The Brightline Customer Support team will introduce a new online appointment option next Monday. Customers who need help with complex account issues can reserve a fifteen-minute video call with a support specialist instead of waiting on the telephone. Appointment times will be available from nine a.m. to six p.m. on weekdays. Before the call, customers will receive a secure link and a short form asking for basic information about the problem. Simple questions can still be handled through live chat. The company will review customer feedback after three months before deciding whether to expand evening appointment hours.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: The Stonebridge Conference Center has added three small meeting rooms for groups of up to twelve people. Each room includes a large screen, video-conference equipment, and a whiteboard. Reservations can be made by the hour or for a full day. Coffee and bottled water are included with full-day reservations, while other refreshments can be ordered separately. Groups that need technical assistance should request support at least one business day in advance. The new rooms are located on the second floor near the elevators. Current rates and available dates are listed on the conference center's reservation page.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: This month, the City Animal Shelter is offering reduced adoption fees for adult cats and dogs. Every adopted animal receives a basic health examination, required vaccinations, and a microchip before leaving the shelter. Potential adopters should bring identification and be prepared to answer questions about their home and daily schedule. Families who already have pets may speak with staff about arranging a safe introduction. The shelter is open from noon until six Tuesday through Sunday. Visitors can view available animals online, but adoption decisions must be completed in person with a staff member.

readAloud.text: Employees who travel for business should use the updated expense form beginning July first. Receipts must be attached for hotel stays, transportation, and individual purchases over twenty-five dollars. Meal expenses should be entered by date rather than combined into one total. Completed reports must be submitted within ten business days after returning from a trip. Managers will receive an email when a report is ready for approval. A short video explaining the new form is available on the finance department website. Questions about unusual expenses should be discussed with Finance before the report is submitted.

readAloud.text: The Downtown Arts Center will offer evening photography classes for beginners starting next month. The six-week course meets every Tuesday from seven to eight thirty and covers basic camera settings, lighting, composition, and simple photo editing. Students may use a digital camera or a smartphone. The instructor will provide weekly practice assignments and review selected photographs during class. Registration includes access to the center's computer lab on class evenings. Space is limited to sixteen students, and early registration is recommended. A complete materials list will be sent by email one week before the first class.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: A new recycling station has been installed beside the employee entrance of the Westgate Factory. Separate containers are available for paper, plastic bottles, metal cans, batteries, and small electronic devices. Employees should remove food and liquids before placing items in the containers. Larger electronics, such as computer monitors, must still be taken to the technology department for proper disposal. Signs above the containers explain which materials are accepted. The company will monitor the program for several months and may add recycling stations in other buildings if participation is high. Thank you for helping us reduce waste.

readAloud.text: The Seaside Visitor Center offers free walking maps and information about local attractions every day from nine until five. Staff can recommend restaurants, hiking routes, museums, and activities for children. Visitors who want to join the historic district walking tour should register at least thirty minutes before departure. Tours leave at ten in the morning and two in the afternoon and last about one hour. Comfortable shoes are recommended because several streets are made of stone. During severe weather, tours may be canceled, so visitors should confirm the schedule by phone before traveling to the center.
readAloud.benchmarkNote: Original practice passage calibrated to the length and workplace/everyday register of the 2025 ETS official sample.

readAloud.text: Next Wednesday, the company cafeteria will host a nutrition information event during lunchtime. A registered dietitian will answer questions about healthy meal choices and explain how to read nutrition labels. Employees can also receive a short printed guide with examples of balanced meals and snacks. The event will take place near the cafeteria entrance from eleven thirty until one thirty, and no registration is required. Several new lunch items will be available for tasting in small portions. Employees with food allergies should check ingredient cards before trying any samples. Everyone is welcome to stop by.

readAloud.text: The North County Transit Office has launched a mobile ticket option for local buses. Riders can purchase single trips or day passes through the transit app and activate a ticket shortly before boarding. Once activated, the ticket must be shown to the driver on the phone screen. Paper tickets and transit cards will continue to be accepted. Riders should make sure their phones have enough battery power for the entire trip because drivers cannot accept screenshots of expired tickets. Instructions for downloading the app and setting up payment are available on buses and at major transit stations.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a local library is conducting a survey about how residents use libraries. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview.

questions.prompt: How often do you visit a library, and when do you usually go?
questions.sampleAnswer: I visit a library about twice a week. I usually go in the late afternoon after class because it is quiet and I can study there for a few hours.

questions.prompt: What do you usually do at the library?
questions.sampleAnswer: I usually study, borrow books, and use the quiet reading area. Sometimes I also reserve a small room when I need to work on a group project.

questions.prompt: What is one service you would like your local library to offer, and why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I would like my local library to offer more evening study rooms. Many students and office workers cannot visit until after dinner, but most reservable rooms close early. For example, during exam season I often need a quiet place after eight o'clock. Longer room hours would make the library much more useful for people with busy daytime schedules.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a food delivery company is researching customers' ordering habits. You have agreed to answer a few questions by telephone.

questions.prompt: How often do you order food for delivery?
questions.sampleAnswer: I order food for delivery about once a week, usually on Friday evening when I am tired and do not feel like cooking.

questions.prompt: What kind of food do you most often order, and why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I most often order Korean food because it travels well and there are many choices near my apartment. It is also easy to share with friends.

questions.prompt: What is the most important thing a food delivery service can do to keep customers satisfied?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think accurate delivery times are the most important. Customers plan their meals around the time shown in the app, so long unexpected delays are frustrating. For example, if an order is going to be thirty minutes late, the service should update the customer immediately. Reliable timing and clear communication would make me much more likely to use the service again.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that your city government is asking residents about public parks. You are taking part in a telephone survey.

questions.prompt: How often do you visit a public park?
questions.sampleAnswer: I visit a public park two or three times a week. I usually go after dinner to walk for about thirty minutes and get some fresh air.

questions.prompt: What activity do you enjoy doing at a park?
questions.sampleAnswer: I enjoy walking the most because it is simple and relaxing. I can exercise lightly while listening to music or talking with a friend.

questions.prompt: What improvement would make public parks in your area more useful?
questions.sampleAnswer: I would add more covered seating areas. The parks near my home have many benches, but most of them are completely exposed to the sun and rain. For example, families often leave quickly when the weather changes. Small covered areas would let people rest, eat, or wait comfortably and would make the parks useful during more kinds of weather.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that an education company is conducting research about online classes. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview.

questions.prompt: How often do you take online classes or watch educational videos?
questions.sampleAnswer: I use online learning materials several times a week. I usually watch short lessons in the evening when I want to review something from class.

questions.prompt: What device do you prefer to use for online learning, and why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I prefer using a laptop because the screen is larger and I can take notes more easily. It is also more convenient when I need several browser windows open.

questions.prompt: What makes an online class effective for you?
questions.sampleAnswer: For me, an effective online class needs short lessons and frequent practice activities. If a video is too long, it is easy to lose concentration. For example, I learn vocabulary better when a ten-minute explanation is followed by a quick quiz. That format helps me check whether I understood the lesson before moving on to the next topic.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that an event company is researching how people choose local festivals and community events. You have agreed to answer several questions.

questions.prompt: How often do you attend local festivals or community events?
questions.sampleAnswer: I attend a local event every couple of months, especially in spring and fall when there are outdoor festivals and the weather is comfortable.

questions.prompt: Who do you usually go to these events with?
questions.sampleAnswer: I usually go with two or three friends because it is more fun to try food, watch performances, and explore different booths together.

questions.prompt: What kind of activity should organizers include to make a community event more enjoyable?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think organizers should include short hands-on activities. People enjoy doing something themselves instead of only watching. For example, a food festival could offer a simple cooking demonstration where visitors prepare one small dish. Activities like that give people something memorable to do and also make it easier for families or groups of friends to participate together.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a transportation company is studying bicycle use in your city. You have agreed to answer questions in a telephone interview.

questions.prompt: How often do you ride a bicycle?
questions.sampleAnswer: I ride a bicycle about once or twice a week. I usually use it on weekends when I have time to exercise or visit a nearby park.

questions.prompt: Where do you usually ride a bicycle?
questions.sampleAnswer: I usually ride along the river because there is a long bicycle path separated from cars. It feels safer and the scenery is much nicer than downtown streets.

questions.prompt: What could your city do to encourage more people to ride bicycles?
questions.sampleAnswer: The city should build more protected bicycle lanes. Many people are interested in cycling, but they feel uncomfortable riding next to fast traffic. For example, I avoid several shopping areas because there is no safe lane connecting them to the river path. A connected network of protected lanes would make cycling safer and more practical for everyday transportation.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a business magazine is researching workplace meetings. You are participating in a telephone survey about meetings at work or school.

questions.prompt: How often do you attend meetings or group discussions?
questions.sampleAnswer: I attend meetings or group discussions about three times a week. Most of them are for class projects, and they usually last thirty to forty minutes.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer in-person meetings or online meetings, and why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I prefer in-person meetings because it is easier to see everyone's reactions and have a natural discussion. I also get distracted less than I do during online meetings.

questions.prompt: What is one way to make meetings more productive?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think every meeting should have a short agenda shared in advance. When people know the topics and decisions that need to be made, they can prepare and stay focused. For example, my project group started listing three discussion points before each meeting, and our meetings became much shorter because we stopped spending time on unrelated issues.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a clothing retailer is researching customers' shopping preferences. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview.

questions.prompt: How often do you buy new clothes?
questions.sampleAnswer: I buy new clothes every two or three months. I usually shop when the season changes or when I need something specific for work or school.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer shopping for clothes online or in a store?
questions.sampleAnswer: I prefer shopping in a store because I can try things on and check the material. That helps me avoid buying clothes that do not fit well.

questions.prompt: What is the most important factor when you decide whether to buy a piece of clothing?
questions.sampleAnswer: The most important factor for me is whether I can wear the item often. I would rather buy one simple jacket that works with many outfits than something fashionable that I can only wear once or twice. For example, I usually choose neutral colors because they are easy to match. That makes the purchase more useful and worth the price.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a home appliance company is researching how customers choose household products. You have agreed to answer a few questions.

questions.prompt: What household appliance do you use most often?
questions.sampleAnswer: I use my electric kettle most often because I make coffee or tea several times a day. It is quick, simple, and easy to clean.

questions.prompt: Where do you usually get information before buying an appliance?
questions.sampleAnswer: I usually compare products online and read customer reviews. I also watch short review videos when I want to see how the appliance works in real use.

questions.prompt: Would you pay more for an appliance that uses less energy? Why or why not?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I would pay somewhat more for an energy-efficient appliance because I would use it for several years. A higher purchase price can be reasonable if it reduces electricity costs every month. For example, when my family replaced an old air conditioner with an efficient model, our summer electricity bill became noticeably lower. The long-term savings can make the extra cost worthwhile.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a travel company is conducting research about hotel stays. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview.

questions.prompt: How often do you stay at a hotel?
questions.sampleAnswer: I stay at a hotel a few times a year, usually during vacations or short weekend trips to another city.

questions.prompt: What hotel feature is most important to you?
questions.sampleAnswer: A convenient location is most important to me because I do not want to spend a lot of time traveling between the hotel and the places I want to visit.

questions.prompt: Describe one hotel service that made a trip more convenient for you.
questions.sampleAnswer: A hotel shuttle made one of my trips much easier. The hotel offered free transportation between the airport and the lobby every hour. I arrived late at night, so I did not have to search for a taxi or figure out public transportation with my luggage. The service saved time, reduced stress, and made the first day of the trip much smoother.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a community center is planning new adult classes. You are taking part in a telephone survey about recreational classes.

questions.prompt: Have you ever taken a class outside of school or work? What was it?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes. Last year I took a beginner cooking class at a community center. It met once a week and focused on simple meals that could be prepared quickly.

questions.prompt: What kind of class would you like to take in the future?
questions.sampleAnswer: I would like to take a photography class because I travel often and want to take better pictures. I especially want to learn about lighting and composition.

questions.prompt: What makes a recreational class worth paying for?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think a class is worth paying for when students get personal feedback and enough time to practice. Information alone is easy to find online. For example, in a cooking class an instructor can watch how I prepare something and correct a mistake immediately. That kind of direct help is difficult to get from a video, so it makes the class more valuable.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a music website is researching people's listening and concert habits. You have agreed to answer several questions.

questions.prompt: How often do you listen to music?
questions.sampleAnswer: I listen to music every day, mostly while commuting or exercising. I probably spend at least an hour a day listening to different playlists.

questions.prompt: What kind of music do you listen to most often?
questions.sampleAnswer: I listen to pop music most often because it is energetic and easy to listen to while I am doing other things like walking or cleaning.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer listening to recorded music or attending a live concert? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I prefer live concerts because the atmosphere makes the music feel much more exciting. Hearing a favorite song with a large audience creates an experience that headphones cannot copy. For example, I attended a small concert last year, and even songs I already knew sounded different because the musicians changed parts of the performance and interacted with the audience.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a bank is researching how customers pay for everyday purchases. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview.

questions.prompt: How do you usually pay for everyday purchases?
questions.sampleAnswer: I usually pay by card or with a mobile payment app. I rarely carry much cash because electronic payment is faster and works at most stores I visit.

questions.prompt: What kind of purchase are you most likely to pay for with cash?
questions.sampleAnswer: I am most likely to use cash at a small street market. Some vendors do not accept cards, and paying a small amount in cash is simple.

questions.prompt: What feature would make a mobile payment service more useful to you?
questions.sampleAnswer: I would like a mobile payment service to organize spending automatically by category. It would be useful if every purchase were labeled as food, transportation, shopping, or another category. For example, at the end of the month I could quickly see where most of my money went. That would make the payment app useful for budgeting as well as for paying.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a cooking magazine is conducting a survey about home cooking. You have agreed to answer several questions by telephone.

questions.prompt: How often do you cook at home?
questions.sampleAnswer: I cook at home four or five times a week. I usually prepare dinner because it is cheaper than eating out and I can make enough for the next day.

questions.prompt: Where do you usually find ideas for meals?
questions.sampleAnswer: I usually find meal ideas on cooking websites and short videos. I like recipes that show the ingredients clearly and take less than thirty minutes.

questions.prompt: What is the best way for a busy person to cook at home more often?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think planning a few meals before shopping is the best method. If the ingredients are already at home, cooking feels much easier after a busy day. For example, I choose three simple dinners on Sunday and buy everything at once. I can also prepare vegetables in advance. This saves time during the week and prevents me from ordering delivery just because I am tired.

interviewGroups.intro: Imagine that a nonprofit organization is researching people's experience with volunteering. You have agreed to take part in a telephone interview.

questions.prompt: Have you ever done volunteer work? What kind?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes. I have volunteered at a neighborhood clean-up event several times. We collected trash, separated recyclable items, and cleaned walking paths in a local park.

questions.prompt: Would you rather volunteer alone or with people you know?
questions.sampleAnswer: I would rather volunteer with people I know because we can encourage each other and the work feels more enjoyable when we can talk while doing it.

questions.prompt: What can organizations do to encourage more young people to volunteer?
questions.sampleAnswer: Organizations should offer short, flexible volunteer opportunities that clearly explain the impact of the work. Young people may want to help but cannot commit every weekend. For example, a two-hour event with online sign-up is much easier to join than a long program. Showing photos or results afterward can also help volunteers see that their time made a real difference.

opinions.prompt: Some companies allow employees to choose flexible starting and ending times instead of requiring everyone to work the same schedule. Do you think flexible work hours are a good idea? Give reasons for your opinion.
opinions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think flexible work hours are a good idea when the job allows them. First, people have different responsibilities and commuting situations, so a flexible schedule can reduce unnecessary stress. For example, a parent may need to take a child to school before coming to work, while another employee may prefer to start early and avoid rush-hour traffic. Second, employees can often work better during the hours when they are most focused. Of course, teams still need common times for meetings and customer service. However, if a company sets clear rules about availability, flexibility can improve both productivity and employee satisfaction. For those reasons, I would support flexible working hours.

opinions.prompt: Do you think companies should spend more money on training current employees or on hiring new employees with the skills they need? Give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
opinions.sampleAnswer: I think companies should spend more money training current employees. Existing employees already understand the company, its customers, and the way the team works, so helping them develop new skills can be efficient. For example, if a company needs workers who understand a new software system, it may be faster to train experienced staff than to hire many new people who also need time to learn the organization. Training can also improve motivation because employees see that the company is willing to invest in their growth. Hiring is still necessary when a company lacks specialized knowledge. However, for skills that can reasonably be taught, developing current employees is usually the better long-term investment.

opinions.prompt: Some cities are considering spending more money on public transportation instead of building additional roads for cars. Which choice do you think is better? Give reasons for your opinion.
opinions.sampleAnswer: I think cities should invest more in public transportation. Good buses and trains can move many people efficiently without requiring every traveler to use a separate car. This can reduce traffic and make commuting more predictable. For example, when a subway line connects residential areas with major business districts, thousands of people can avoid driving during rush hour. Public transportation is also important for students, older residents, and people who cannot afford a car. Roads still need maintenance, and some areas depend on cars. However, continuously adding roads often creates more traffic over time. A reliable transportation network gives residents more choices and can make a city easier and less expensive to travel around.

opinions.prompt: When completing an important project, do you prefer working as part of a team or working independently? Give reasons and examples to support your choice.
opinions.sampleAnswer: For an important project, I prefer working as part of a small team. Different people can contribute different strengths, so the final result is often better than one person's work. For example, on a presentation project, one person may be good at research, another at visual design, and another at speaking. A team can also notice mistakes that an individual might overlook. Of course, teamwork requires communication, and too many people can make decisions slower. That is why I prefer a small group with clear responsibilities. If everyone understands what they need to do and shares progress regularly, a team can work efficiently while still benefiting from several perspectives. For me, that is the best balance.

opinions.prompt: Some people prefer buying products from large national stores, while others prefer shopping at small local businesses. Which do you prefer, and why?
opinions.sampleAnswer: I prefer shopping at small local businesses when the price and quality are reasonable. One reason is that local stores often provide more personal service. Employees may know their products well and can recommend something based on what a customer actually needs. I also like knowing that some of the money I spend stays in the local community. For example, there is a small bakery near my home, and the owner remembers regular customers and adjusts the menu based on their feedback. Large stores are useful because they usually have more choices and lower prices. Still, for everyday purchases where service and quality matter, I enjoy supporting smaller businesses and building a relationship with the people who run them.

opinions.prompt: Do you think taking notes by hand is better than taking notes on a computer or tablet? Give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
opinions.sampleAnswer: I think taking notes by hand is better for learning, although digital notes are more convenient for storage. When I write by hand, I have to choose the most important ideas instead of copying everything quickly. That process helps me pay attention and remember the material. For example, before an exam, I often remember the page where I wrote a diagram or a key formula. Handwritten notes also reduce distractions because I am not receiving messages or opening other websites. Digital notes are useful when I need to search, organize, or share information. However, during a lecture or study session, I understand the content better when I write the main points myself. Therefore, I usually prefer handwritten notes.

opinions.prompt: Do you think every new employee should be assigned an experienced coworker as a mentor during the first few months? Why or why not?
opinions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think new employees should have a mentor during their first few months. Starting a new job involves many small questions that may not be covered in formal training. A mentor can explain normal procedures, introduce important coworkers, and help the new employee understand how the team communicates. For example, a new worker might know how to use the company's software but still be unsure about who approves a certain request. Asking one assigned person is faster than trying to find the answer alone. Mentoring also helps new employees feel more comfortable and connected. The mentor should not do the new employee's work, but regular guidance at the beginning can prevent mistakes and help people become independent more quickly.

opinions.prompt: For business meetings with people in another city or country, do you think video calls are usually better than traveling in person? Give reasons for your opinion.
opinions.sampleAnswer: For most routine business meetings, I think video calls are better than traveling in person. They save both time and money because employees do not need flights, hotels, or long trips to the airport. A one-hour meeting can actually take only one hour instead of an entire day. For example, project teams can hold a quick video meeting every week and solve problems before they become serious. In-person meetings are still valuable when people are building a new relationship, negotiating an important agreement, or visiting a work site. However, those situations do not happen every day. For regular updates and discussions, video calls are efficient and allow companies to communicate frequently without the cost and environmental impact of constant travel.

opinions.prompt: Do you think university students should be required to complete an internship or other work experience before graduation? Give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
opinions.sampleAnswer: I think university students should complete some type of work experience before graduation, although the requirement should be flexible. An internship helps students understand how knowledge from class is used in a real workplace. It can also show them which jobs they actually enjoy. For example, a student studying marketing may discover during an internship that they prefer data analysis to advertising. Work experience also teaches practical skills such as professional communication, deadlines, and teamwork. Some students may not be able to take a traditional full-time internship, so universities should also accept part-time projects, research work, or community organizations. With several options available, a work-experience requirement could help students make better career decisions and enter the job market with more confidence.

opinions.prompt: Some cities use empty land for new buildings, while others preserve it as parks or green spaces. Which choice do you think is more important for a growing city?
opinions.sampleAnswer: I think growing cities should preserve enough land for parks and green spaces. New buildings are necessary, but once open land is completely developed, it can be very difficult to create large public spaces later. Parks give residents places to exercise, relax, and spend time with family without paying money. For example, a neighborhood park can be used by children in the afternoon, runners in the evening, and community events on weekends. Green areas can also provide shade and make dense neighborhoods more comfortable during hot weather. Cities still need housing and offices, so development cannot stop. However, planning should include parks from the beginning. A city with both useful buildings and accessible green spaces is healthier and more pleasant to live in.

opinions.prompt: What is a better way for a company to reward excellent employees: giving them extra money or giving them additional time off? Give reasons for your choice.
opinions.sampleAnswer: I think extra money is usually the better reward for excellent employees because it gives people more freedom to decide what is valuable to them. One employee might use the money for travel, while another might save it or pay an important expense. A financial reward also clearly recognizes that the person's work created value for the company. For example, if an employee successfully completes a difficult project that brings in a new client, a bonus feels directly connected to that achievement. Additional time off can also be very attractive, especially for employees who are already financially comfortable. However, not everyone can use extra vacation at the same time. Because money is flexible and easy to understand, I would choose a bonus as a reward.

opinions.prompt: When choosing a restaurant or hotel, how important are online customer reviews? Do you think people should rely on them? Give reasons for your opinion.
opinions.sampleAnswer: I think online reviews are useful, but people should not rely on them completely. Reviews can show common patterns that are difficult to see from an advertisement. For example, if many recent guests mention that a hotel is clean and close to public transportation, that information is probably helpful. However, individual reviews can be extremely positive or negative because of one unusual experience. Some reviews may also be old or may focus on things that are not important to me. I usually read several recent comments and look for repeated points instead of trusting one person's opinion. Then I compare that information with the official website, location, and price. Reviews are a good research tool, but they should be only one part of the decision.

opinions.prompt: Do you think living or studying in another country is one of the best ways to learn about a different culture? Why or why not?
opinions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think living or studying in another country is one of the best ways to learn about a different culture because people experience daily life directly. They learn not only about famous traditions but also about ordinary habits, communication styles, transportation, food, and work or school routines. For example, a student living with local roommates may learn how people normally celebrate small holidays or solve everyday problems. Books and videos can provide useful background, and not everyone has the opportunity to travel. Still, direct experience forces people to communicate and adapt in real situations. It can also challenge assumptions they had before arriving. For those reasons, spending meaningful time in another country can create a deeper understanding than simply reading about it.

opinions.prompt: Some people work or study for long periods without stopping, while others take short scheduled breaks. Which approach do you think is more effective?
opinions.sampleAnswer: I think short scheduled breaks are more effective than working for several hours without stopping. Concentration naturally decreases over time, so a brief break can help people return to a task with more energy. For example, when I study for about fifty minutes and then walk around for ten minutes, I can focus much better during the next session. Breaks can also prevent small physical problems such as eye strain or stiffness from sitting too long. Of course, breaks should be controlled. If someone spends thirty minutes checking social media, it can be difficult to start working again. A simple schedule with focused work periods and short breaks creates a good balance between productivity and rest. That approach works best for me.

opinions.prompt: Do you think companies should organize paid volunteer days when employees can work on community projects instead of doing their normal jobs? Give reasons for your opinion.
opinions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think companies should offer a limited number of paid volunteer days. Community projects can help organizations contribute to the places where their employees and customers live. They can also create a different kind of teamwork. For example, employees from several departments might spend a day preparing food at a community center or cleaning a public park. Working together outside the office can help people know coworkers they normally do not meet. The program should be optional, and companies still need to manage important deadlines. However, one or two volunteer days a year would not create a major disruption for most businesses. If the projects are organized well, both the community and the employees can benefit.
